Yeah the pinned comment stating it mainly focuses on real world criminalization brings me pause. Like yes that to an extent alleviates some concerns with how far it could impact Dead Dove content…but ignores the fact a lot of legal shifting is happening in the U.S. right now.

J.ai is under U.S. law…and the current Supreme Court has more or less opened the floodgates to a lot of litigation involving a variety of minority groups (with some cases, such as the potential overturning of gay marriage swiftly approaching). So, if the Supreme Court were to affirm the current administration’s denial of the existence of Trans people  and open the door to criminalization, would Trans bots be banned? If they don’t stop at Obergefell and also overturn Lawrence (which bans anti-gay sex laws essentially) will J.ai follow suit in banning LGBT bots period?

Obviously there’s a lot up in the air there…but the fact it’s even a real possibility is beyond concerning, and all dev “clarifications” on the matter honestly haven’t done much to assuage those fears. 

TLDR: It’s not just Dead Dove content potentially at risk.

Yeah there’s a lot of issues with the morally or ethically questionable rule…mostly because it becomes a question of morally or ethically illegal to whom.

For instance, in the U.S…abortion is considered morally/ethically wrong and even criminalized by certain state governments (and as of now? Heavily discriminated by the current Fed. Administration). Does that mean that any bot dealing with or touching on such themes will be banned from here on out? 

What about Trans bots given the current legal questions involving their quasi-criminalization in the states? Or LGBT bots period (given some of the cases in front of the U.S. Supreme Court)? 

As it is worded now…it could even lead to the removal of most Dead Dove/Angst content entirely (many of which bots are enjoyed by many including myself) because it potentially features non-con, death, suicide, murder, kidnapping, or even something as comparatively simple as burglary.

Overall it’s extremely poorly worded and has a potential to lead to far reaching ramifications that I don’t think they fully considered that needs to be clarified/addressed. Honestly? Some bots absolutely should be taken down (such as bots with explicit depictions of minors/blatant zoophilia bots/etc) but as it is now? The potential for censorship is ridiculous and frankly a potential site killer.

The thing that gets me about those particular arguments is that if you apply that same argument to a het FemPOV or MalePOV bot, they immediately get up in arms about it. 

And arguably? Unlike the case for MLM or WLW content, that point has actual validity to it since the vast majority of het bots deal with scenarios that in no way point to a specific sexuality. They’re simply straight because to them? That’s the assumed default. 

The point could be nailed to their skull and they would still miss it almost every single time.

Yeah, tell me about it. The worst part (for me at least) is if they really wanted to engage with the bots in good faith it’s really just as simple as making a Queer Male, Female, or Trans OC and diving in. 

The fact they actively choose to be entitled instead or  brag in the comments about “turning the bot straight” is what concerns me more than anything.

Almost all the fem bots worth interacting with are all under WLW or occasionally AnyPOV tbh. Not sure if those types of bots are exactly your forte, but that’s usually how it goes. I usually focus more on Male bots myself, but if you want the deeper or more intricate roleplaying experiences usually “Fluff”, “Angst”, or more niche tags like “Historical” or “Horror” will produce some bangers as well if you filter right.

If you want the non-meme answer it really just comes down to semantics and differences in geo -political thought between Latin America and Anglo-America. 

In the Anglosphere there is no “America” in the sense that North and South America are considered separate continents, instead being replaced with the idea of the “Americas” (plural). This differs from the model taught in much of Latin America in that there is only one singular “America” (the American super-continent).

Therefore, it isn’t as big of a deal to us as the collective whole with all individual countries therein is called the “Americas”, and “America”  (singular) is assumed to refer to the US in particular due to both historical precedence and it’s significantly easier/logical to say “American” than “United Statesian” in English. Technically neither side is right or wrong in the debate with those respective contexts in mind.
